blocks.x: Compute and delivery close to users and devices: regional clusters with store-and-forward resilience, fleet operations across heterogeneous hardware, rollout waves that respect site windows — and monitors that notice when a site goes silent instead of assuming it is fine.
The edge is defined by its failures: partitions, silence and heterogeneity

Edge is where the cloud's assumptions break: networks partition, power flickers, hardware is diverse, and nobody is there to reboot the box. Edge infrastructure is fleet engineering — regional clusters with autonomous degradation, store-and-forward data paths, and deployment tooling that treats a hundred sites like one release train.

The practice spans the regional tier (metro clusters and CDN), the site tier (factory/store boxes), device gateways, and the fleet operations that keep hundreds of nodes observable and upgradable from one console.
Below: the failure modes that make edge estates fragile, the reference architecture of partition-tolerant design, and the console that keeps a thousand sites honest.
Four failure modes that make edge estates fragile
Each of these hides behind scale — a thousand sites make wonderful averages and terrible individual failures — the countermeasures measure sites as individuals.

blocks.x: Reference architecture — regional clusters with store-and-forward

Sites survive isolation by design: local decision-making on regional clusters, store-and-forward queues that reconcile on reconnect, rollout waves that respect site windows, and heartbeats that make silence a monitored state rather than an assumption.

nodes.label: Edge sites
nodes.detail: Declarative site config under gitops; drift corrected automatically; a site that cannot reach the controller keeps the last-known-good config.

nodes.label: Edge runtime
nodes.detail: Lightweight orchestration sized to silicon; mesh controller features disabled where they cannot degrade gracefully.

nodes.label: Offline services
nodes.detail: Local decision services with bounded-staleness contracts — each declares what it decides without the WAN and for how long.

nodes.label: Sensor fabric
nodes.detail: Instrument capture with local buffering; sensor health is part of the site contract, not an afterthought.

nodes.label: Store-and-forward
nodes.detail: Batched, compressed, prioritized upload — safety events jump the queue; conflicts resolve by declared domain rules, not last-write accidents.

nodes.label: Reconciliation
nodes.detail: Totals matched both ends daily; any delta blocks the site's config updates until explained.

nodes.label: Cloud control
nodes.detail: Fleet observability over 2 Mbps links — metrics downsampled at the edge, traces sampled, dashboards site-scoped.

nodes.label: Model delivery
nodes.detail: Models built centrally, staged per silicon class, rolled out with site cohorts and automatic rollback on regression.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read the offline contract each layer offers. The sync plane is where edge programs live or die.
